vulnerabilities.description: Command Injection: ghCommand constructed by joining user-supplied args without shell escaping. Attackers can inject arbitrary shell commands.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Body parameter contains: '; rm -rf / ; echo '. Results in arbitrary shell command execution.

vulnerabilities.description: Command Injection: execSync runs git config with shell interpretation. Malicious git user.name (e.g., '$(malicious_command)') executes arbitrary code.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Git user.name set to '$(whoami > /tmp/pwned)' causes code execution when statusline queries it.

vulnerabilities.description: Hardcoded Credential Handling: X_USERNAME and X_PASSWORD passed in plaintext via environment variables, exposed in process memory and logs.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Process memory dump or log exposure reveals X credentials used for authentication.

vulnerabilities.description: Insecure Session Storage: Browser session state including auth tokens stored in plaintext JSON file without encryption. World-readable by default.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Attacker reads ${userDataDir}/state.json, extracts session cookies/tokens, hijacks X.com session.

vulnerabilities.description: Insecure Temp File Handling: Temporary files created in world-readable tmpdir without restrictive permissions. Race condition between creation and use.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Another user on system reads temp file before deletion, obtaining API response bodies or command input.

vulnerabilities.description: Missing Authentication/Authorization: No access control on agent spawning or task routing. Any code can execute arbitrary tasks.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Unauthorized actor spawns agents and routes sensitive tasks without user verification.

vulnerabilities.description: OAuth Tokens in Memory: Access/refresh tokens stored in plaintext memory objects. Could be extracted via memory disclosure.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Debugger or memory dump reveals valid OAuth tokens used for authentication bypass.

vulnerabilities.description: Insecure In-Memory Secrets: MemorySecretsProvider stores secrets in plaintext JavaScript Maps without memory protection.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Process memory analysis extracts plaintext secrets stored in development/test scenarios deployed to production.

vulnerabilities.description: Plaintext Data Storage: Memory helper saves unencrypted JSON without validation. Could contain API keys, credentials, personal data.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Attacker reads .claude-flow/data/memory.json, extracts stored API keys or business intelligence.

vulnerabilities.description: Weak Session IDs: Sessions generated using predictable Date.now() instead of cryptographic randomness.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Attacker guesses session ID (known timestamp ±1ms), hijacks user session without authentication.

vulnerabilities.description: Unsafe JSON.parse: No try-catch on JSON.parse. Malformed input throws unhandled exceptions leaking error info.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Attacker sends invalid JSON triggering parse error. Exception message reveals internal state or causes DoS.

vulnerabilities.description: Credentials Logged in Plaintext: Credentials passed to Playwright methods could be captured in debug logs.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Debug logs or Playwright traces expose username/password in plaintext files.

vulnerabilities.description: Unencrypted Vector Embeddings: HNSW embeddings store encoded campaign/creative data in memory without encryption.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Vector embeddings extracted and analyzed to reverse-engineer business strategy or sensitive campaigns.

vulnerabilities.description: Permissive HTML Type: 'html' creative type allows raw HTML without sanitization, leading to XSS if rendered.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Attacker submits creative with HTML type containing <script>alert('xss')</script>, executes in browser.

recommendations: Immediately patch command injection vulnerabilities using array-based exec (e.g., execSync(['git', 'config', 'user.name']))
Replace password auth with OAuth2; store tokens in OS keychain (Keychain, Credential Manager, Secret Service)
Encrypt all sensitive data at rest using AES-256; use Google Secret Manager or AWS Secrets Manager for production
Implement role-based access control (RBAC) with authentication/authorization on all agent operations
Use cryptographic session IDs (crypto.randomBytes) instead of Date.now()
Add try-catch around JSON.parse; never log credentials or sensitive data
Run 'npm audit' and implement SAST/SCA tools (Semgrep, Snyk) in CI/CD pipeline
Restrict temporary file permissions to 0o600; encrypt session storage
Remove or sanitize 'html' creative type using DOMPurify if needed
Implement secure logging with field masking for sensitive data
